### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 58 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dbef6af8a72d06ba49d2b207e49db34eab8308e0` — the merge of head `c126efd64cfbedd2a534d2e91a045feba00cc695` into base `a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dbef6af8a72d06ba49d2b207e49db34eab8308e0 && git checkout dbef6af8a72d06ba49d2b207e49db34eab8308e0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d c126efd64cfbedd2a534d2e91a045feba00cc695 && git checkout -B drift-repro a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d && git merge --no-ff c126efd64cfbedd2a534d2e91a045feba00cc695

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `85c411c82c5a98c5da4a7ac0b8429a5dcd87e8ee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts

Inputs read: card #33689 (body, including its `## Amendment` section, and comments 6890539808, 6890670880, 6891502025), PR #33725 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Code read to judge, not reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` :2975-3095, `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` :1-55 and :395-516, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` :1270-1300 and :2085-2125, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` :2470-2530 and :2690-2755, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts`.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-15T08:14Z: 18 success, 10 skipped, 16 still in progress, 0 failed. Success includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Dogfood Regression Gate. Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Live E2E UI. The gate families that judge the pin test, the generated baselines and the registry generation had therefore NOT answered when this record was written.

### ① Derived judgments

- Three new exports on `@objectstack/spec/contracts`: `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY (const)`, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REFUSAL_REASONS (const)`, `ActionConfirmationRefusalReason (type)`. Additive. Right as a surface change. `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` carry exactly these three, with the right kinds and origin `src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, in sorted position. Right.
- `ActionConfirmationRequiredDetails.reason?`: one new optional member, typed to the closed tuple. Additive for a reader; a producer that omits it still compiles. Right. It is not a name-level export, so its absence from the baselines is right.
- Accept set: no schema, no parser and no door changes. Nothing an author writes is refused or rewritten. Right.
- No error-ledger change: every reason rides `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`. Right, and it matches the live gate (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_CODE` / `_STATUS`, `action-execution.ts`).
- The closed five-member reason tuple is itself a published accept set. Publishing it closed, with `elicitation_unsupported` meaning "refused", is wrong against the card as it now reads: see ④ F1. A closed set that has to change in the next card is a second breaking change.
- Semantic entry: the file name is `18.` plus the entry id, which is the rule in `entries/README.md` ("named by protocol major, then the id, then `.ts`"). The `18.` prefix is the protocol major, not an ordinal: 500+ entries share it, `18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts` among them, so a shared prefix is legal and expected. Registration is the file alone (no index, `registry.ts` is generated and git-ignored); the id is unique in the tree; the changeset marker `adr-0087: registered action-requires-confirmation-elicited` names it. Right. No `relevantWhen`, so the entry is always listed; right for a surface that lives at a runtime door.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`: the meaning of an authorable key (`ai.requiresConfirmation: true`) changes and nothing is refused at authoring, so `semantic` is the right kind, and a kind takes at least `minor`. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: `yes` is right, the diff enlarges the published surface by three exports and one member. `(narrowing)` is right, the contract takes a working call shape away (the caller's `confirm: true`). The claim's expected `no (narrowing)` was wrong for this diff and the dev's deviation is correct. Both lines stand line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body. Check Changeset: success.
- The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 disposition marker and a FROM → TO note. The form is right. The content of the FROM → TO is wrong against the amended card (F1) and misleading for the release that carries it (F4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, `Clause-②` changed from the claim: accepted (② above).
- Dev deviation, `Part of #33689` in place of `Refs`: accepted; neither closes the card. PR-body guards: success.
- Dev deviation, the semantic entry file beyond the claim's file surface: accepted; the order allowed it and a FROM → TO note needs a registered disposition.
- Claim boundary "no runtime or MCP behaviour change on this card": held. The diff is six files, all under `packages/spec` plus the changeset.
- ESCALATED to the seat, blocking: the card body carries a `## Amendment (the owner, after the card was filed)` section that changes the rule (pending-confirmation service before any refusal). The claim (6890670880), the dev report (6891502025) and the PR body do not mention it, so the dev was almost certainly ordered against the pre-amendment card. The section sits below the body's `signed:` marker and REST shows no edit history, so its time and author are not verifiable from here; the seat confirms its provenance. This review judges the card as it reads.
- Open question 1 (in-app assistant door): decide before THIS PR lands, or the PR must say plainly that the question is open. The card says "an AI door"; rule 1 closes that to the two MCP tools and the bounds section lists the delete tools and REST but is silent on the in-app assistant. The amendment's pending-confirmation service is the in-app approval queue (`ai_pending_actions` / `proposePendingAction`), so the amended contract cannot be written without naming that door's place.
- Open question 2 (MCP `delete_record` / `delete_records`): not needed for this PR. The contract states the bound truthfully ("until a decision moves them"). Decide before, or as, its own card.
- Open question 3 (the stateless HTTP door cannot elicit): split. What a call does on a door or client that cannot elicit is contract, the amendment has already answered it (hand to the pending-confirmation service; refuse only where the host has none), and it must be right in THIS PR (F1, F3). HOW the HTTP door comes to elicit (options A / B) is implementation and is needed only before the implementing card. Option C as written ("ship refusing on HTTP") is no longer available under the amendment.
- Open question 4 (the `confirm` member on the `run_action` / `resume_run` input schemas): needed only before the implementing card. Note for that decision: the same file still says a door "never accepts-and-ignores" the member (`AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` docblock), and `confirmationMember` stays a required field of the refusal details, telling an agent which member to set on a refusal where setting it does nothing.
- Dev out-of-scope finding (the shipped texts that teach the member move with the implementing card): agreed, carrier is the implementing card.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1, must-fix. The contract publishes the pre-amendment rule; the card now rules the opposite for a client without `elicitation`.** (`ai-service.ts` rule 3, the paragraph after rule 6, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REFUSAL_REASONS`; the entry's `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`; the pin test's remedy regex and "exactly five" case; the changeset's FROM → TO.)
The card's amendment: (1) a client that advertised `elicitation` is elicited; (2) otherwise the action is handed to the host's pending-confirmation service and the caller is answered with a pending id and a plain message, the person approves or rejects in the app (inbox plus an emailed link), and the action then runs as that person with permissions re-checked; (3) refuse only when the host has no pending-confirmation service. It adds that the approve and reject doors refuse an AI identity and that "the contract names the hand-off seam".
The head says: "A client that did not advertise it is REFUSED before anything is asked or run"; "A door that cannot carry an elicitation to the client refuses the same way"; "Nothing is parked or queued, as before"; reason `elicitation_unsupported`: "Retrying from that client cannot succeed". The entry and the changeset tell every consumer the same, and the changeset's second FROM → TO line says "no replacement". None of the head names the hand-off seam, the pending answer's shape, the re-check of permissions at approval, or the AI-identity refusal on the approve and reject doors. The pin test then pins the superseded sentence.
This is not a wording gap. It is the difference between gated actions being unavailable to every hosted caller and being approvable from a phone. The dev's own measurement shows why: the only door that can elicit as built is stdio, and OAuth and API-key callers of a hosted deployment arrive on the stateless HTTP door. Fix: rewrite rule 3, the answer cases, the reason set (a pending outcome is not a refusal; the remaining refusal is "no pending-confirmation service"), the entry, the changeset and the pins to the amended rule.

**F2, should-fix. Rule 2 and the closing paragraph cannot both hold against the live sequence.** (`ai-service.ts` rule 2: "After every other admission gate has passed, so nobody is asked to confirm a call that is refused anyway"; closing paragraph: "a refused call did not run, and no record was read or written for it".)
In `action-dispatch.ts` the confirmation gate is deliberately "the last pre-dispatch check ... before the subject load, so a refusal reads and writes nothing" (:454-471). A refusal comes after it and needs the record: the caller-scope subject verdict (`refuseDeniedSubjectLoadBeforeDispatch`, :511), which follows the subject load at :476. So either the elicitation stays where the gate is, and a person can be asked to confirm a call that is then refused for an unreadable record, or it moves after the subject load, and a declined call has read a record. The contract must pick one and say it. Rule 2 also wants the message to name "the record it runs on": by id that needs no read; by title it does.

**F3, should-fix. The HTTP sentence describes a window the same section says does not exist, and it pre-decides open question 3.** ("When it binds", last paragraph: the stateless Streamable HTTP door "as built ... holds neither, and by rule 3 it refuses until the implementing change gives it both".)
The facts are right: a fresh server per POST, `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`, `enableJsonResponse: true`, GET 405 (`mcp-server-runtime.ts` :2732-2751); the stdio server is long-lived and does hold both. The conclusion is not. Two paragraphs earlier the doors "still gate on the member" until the implementing change, and that change is what "gives it both", so there is no time at which the HTTP door refuses under rule 3, unless the doors switch before the transport does, which is option C of an undecided question. Today the HTTP door runs a gated action on `confirm: true`; the sentence reads as if it already refuses. Under F1 the outcome for that door is a hand-off, not a refusal. Fix with F1: state what the door does today, and leave the transport to the implementing card.

**F4, should-fix. The semantic entry tells a consumer to do, now, what breaks them in the release that carries it.** (`18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`; the same in the changeset's first FROM → TO line, "send no `confirm`".)
`os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide print this entry from the release that ships it. Its body is present tense: "A client that did not advertise ... is refused", "The caller's own `confirm: true` no longer confirms anything", "A script or agent that sent `confirm: true` ... stops working by design: it is refused", "Done when no caller relies on its own `confirm: true`". In that release the live gate is `request?.[AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER] === true` (`action-execution.ts` :3077): `confirm: true` is the only thing that runs a gated action, no door elicits, and a caller that follows the criteria and drops the member is refused 428 on every gated action. The one hedge is the last sentence of `replacement`. `ai-service.ts` says the lead plainly in "When it binds"; the entry does not. Fix: lead the entry with the timing and make the criteria conditional on the door having switched, or land the entry and the BREAKING banner with the implementing card, where they are true.

**F5, nit. The trust bound is no longer stated.** The member contract was candid ("an unverifiable claim", "did not prove a person"). The amended text says the server "asks the person, through the client" and "An agent cannot answer for the person by sending it". Both are true of the member. But an elicitation answer proves that the client answered, not that a person did: a caller's own client can advertise `elicitation` and return `accept`, which rule 6 admits for a service account ("its own client could answer one") and not for an API-key script. One sentence stating that bound keeps the next reader, and the ADR notes, from reading the contract as proof of a human.

**F6, nit. Which doors set `reason: 'service_account'` is ambiguous.** `reason` is set by "every door implementing that contract"; rule 1 scopes the contract to two MCP tools; the service-account refusal also fires on REST `/actions` and host doors (`action-dispatch.ts` :460). Say whether those refusals carry the reason.

**F7, nit. The `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` amended paragraph reads as present fact** ("is now a person's answer ... the member never counts on such a call"), with the timing only behind a link. `AIActionConfirmation`'s own amended paragraph does this better ("the doors enforce until the change that implements the amendment"); use the same wording.

What holds and needs no change: the description of the member contract as the FROM half; the predicate (the DECLARED flag); the service-account rule and its ADR-0151 D3 rule 3 citation, which match `isAiServiceAccountCaller` and the gate; `resume_run` "for the candidate action it would run", which matches `resumeAdmissionRefusal`; the bounds on the delete tools and REST; "an empty `elicitation: {}` reads as form mode (MCP 2025-11-25)"; the accept / decline / cancel / timed-out cases for the elicited path, which the amendment keeps.

Pin test (`action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts`), against the contract: it agrees with the head's text sentence by sentence (the capability spelling, the five reasons in order, the typed optional `reason` with its `ts-expect-error` leg, no second ledger code, the docblock naming each reason and answer). It therefore pins F1's superseded rule in two places, the "exactly five" tuple and the remedy regex, and moves with the F1 fix. It pins no door behaviour and says so. Test Core had not concluded at the time of this record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c0ebf0c35bbbebb02860e107d4d58f052f67b613`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts

Delta review, round 2. Round 1 was FAIL on `85c411c8` (record 6891568840); the seat ruled on it in card comment 6891575459, and the card body's `## Amendment` governs. This record states, for each round-1 finding, whether it is resolved at this head, then judges the text round 2 introduced.

Inputs read: card #33689 (body with its `## Amendment`, and comments 6890539808, 6890670880, 6891502025, 6891575459, 6892233660), PR #33725 (body as rewritten for round 2, file list, the net diff of the six files against the PR's base), and the check-runs on the head. Code read to judge, not reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` :395-520, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` :2975-3095, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` :1935-2125 (`resume_run`), `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` :3296-3350 and :3461-3550 (the two tool inputs), `packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts` (`principalKind`, `onBehalfOf`), `packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts` :18-30, the unchanged `IAIService` pending-action members in `ai-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md`.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-15T09:24Z: 71 runs, 0 failed, 0 in progress; every run is success or skipped. Success includes Check Changeset and PR-body guards (both also re-run green after the PR body was rewritten at 09:20Z), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · source gates / workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Dogfood Regression Gate. The families that judge the pin test, the generated baselines and the registry generation have answered, which they had not in round 1.

### ① Derived judgments

- Six new exports on `@objectstack/spec/contracts`: `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY (const)`, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REFUSAL_REASONS (const)`, `ActionConfirmationRefusalReason (type)`, `ActionConfirmationHandOff (interface)`, `ActionConfirmationPending (interface)`, `IActionConfirmationService (interface)`. Additive. `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` carry exactly these six, right kinds, origin `src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, sorted. Right.
- `ActionConfirmationRequiredDetails.reason?`: one optional member typed to the closed tuple. Additive. Right.
- The closed reason tuple is now `declined`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `no_confirmation_service`, `service_account`. Right against the amended card: a hand-off is a success answer and is not in it, and `elicitation_unsupported` is gone. The round-1 objection to this accept set is answered.
- `ActionConfirmationPending.status` is the single literal `pending_confirmation`. Right (see ③).
- `ActionConfirmationHandOff` is a published input shape a host implements against. Its member set is wrong for one of the two doors the contract names: see ④ N1.
- Accept set of authored metadata: unchanged. No schema, parser or door changes; nothing an author writes is refused or rewritten. Right.
- No error-ledger change: every refusal rides `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`. Right, and it matches the live gate.
- Semantic entry: file name `18.` plus the id, registered by the file alone, id unique, changeset marker `adr-0087: registered action-requires-confirmation-elicited`. Right, as in round 1.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Right: the meaning of `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` changes, nothing is refused at authoring.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Right: the surface grows by six exports and one member, and the contract takes the caller's `confirm: true` away. The line stands line-initial in the PR body and the changeset and now lists all six names. Check Changeset: success.
- The changeset's FROM and TO lines are rewritten to the amended rule; "no replacement" is gone, and the BREAKING banner now reads "when the implementing change ships". Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Seat ruling 6891575459 "Unchanged" list (`Clause-②`, `Metadata-protocol`, minor, entry `18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts`, PR 1 spec-only): held. The diff is the same six files, all under `packages/spec` plus the changeset.
- Dev deviation, the literal `pending_confirmation` in place of the chat envelope's `pending_approval`: accepted. `IAIService.proposePendingAction` in this same file documents `{ status: 'pending_approval' }` as the envelope the in-app tool handler returns to the model, with a different shape and a door the contract is ruled silent on (Q1). A second answer under the same literal would make the two indistinguishable to a reader of `status`. The word also agrees with the scenario grader's existing `pending_confirmation` outcome ("the write waits on a person's confirmation"), which is not published contract.
- Dev deviation, the reading of "AI identity" (an agent principal with or without `onBehalfOf`, plus any call through an AI door): accepted in what it includes, which is wider than the service account alone and right. NOT accepted as complete: it leaves one caller the contract itself covers. See ④ N2.
- Dev deviation, `IActionConfirmationService` not added to the core service registry: accepted for `CoreServiceName`, which is outside the file surface. The lookup name is still owed by the contract, and a precedent inside the file surface exists. See ④ N3.
- Dev deviation, a refusal at approval recorded on the pending item: accepted; it is the only place a person who approved would see it.
- Dev deviations, two commits without a force-push and `main` not merged: accepted; the PR reads mergeable and clean.
- Open question 1 (the in-app assistant door): answered as the seat ruled. The PR body states it OPEN; rule 1 names the two MCP tools only and no new sentence speaks for the in-app door.
- Open questions 2, 3 and 4: routed to the implementing card by the seat. The contract's bounds section keeps the delete tools on the member, and "When it binds" leaves how the HTTP door comes to elicit to that card. Held.
- ESCALATED to the seat with N2: whether the approve and reject doors must take a person's signed-in session (the card's "The person signs in") is the card's rule to confirm, since tightening it past "refuse an AI identity" changes what a host builds.

### ④ Design judgment

Round-1 findings at this head:

- **F1 (must-fix): resolved.** Rule 3 is the three steps in order, "A door or a client that cannot elicit is never refused for that alone", and "No step ever falls back to the member". The seam is named as an optional host service (`IActionConfirmationService.submit`), the pending answer has a shape, the re-check at approval and the AI-identity refusal on the approve and reject doors are stated, no cloud store name is imported, and `held` is cited as precedent in the words its own docblock uses. The reason set, the entry, the changeset and the pins moved with it. Two defects in the new seam text are N1 and N2 below.
- **F2 (should-fix): resolved.** Rule 2 picks the ordering: after every admission gate, the subject load and the caller-scope verdict included, and before dispatch; "may therefore have READ its subject ... it writes nothing". "No record was read" is gone and pinned absent. The elicitation names the record by id, and by title only when the load read one. This is a change from the live order (`action-dispatch.ts` :454-471 asks before the load) and the text says it as the rule the implementing change moves to.
